I am starting work on a new issue. I will list it below. Is the story clear enough to implement? Do not make any changes yet, let me know if anything needs to be cleared up. If not, let me know the plan for the code changes and how it fits in with the structure of the project.

<pasted_content id="f4ef">
User Story

As a store manager, I want to offer products as recurring subscriptions, so that customers can automatically receive and pay for products on a regular schedule without placing a new order each time.

User Scenario

A store manager marks a product as subscribable and sets an available interval (e.g. monthly). A customer purchases the product as a subscription instead of a one-time order. On each interval, the system automatically creates a new order and charges the customer's saved payment method, continuing until the customer cancels or the subscription otherwise ends.

Acceptance Criteria

A product (or variant) can be configured as subscription-eligible, with one or more supported intervals (weekly/monthly/yearly)
A customer can purchase a subscription-eligible product on a recurring basis instead of (or alongside) a one-time purchase
The system automatically generates a new order and charges the customer at each interval
A customer can view and cancel an active subscription
Failed recurring payments are handled (retry and/or subscription status change) rather than silently failing
Subscriptions are tied to existing customer and order systems

Out of Scope

Storefront UI for subscription management (this ticket covers backend/core capability)
Proration, mid-cycle plan changes, or upgrade/downgrade flows
Usage-based or metered billing
Multi-product/bundled subscriptions

Open Questions

How does this integrate with existing payment providers: do they support recurring charges natively, or does Medusa need to build its own scheduling/retry layer?
What happens to a subscription when a product is discontinued or its price changes?
Is subscription state modeled as a new core module, or as a plugin/extension on top of existing commerce modules?

Source

#2942 of the Medusa discussions

```text
Issue 38 (branch feat/issue-38-relevant-suggestions) adds a Store API endpoint suggesting the top-seller in a cart item's category. Follow-up to issue 37 (PR #43, `GET /store/carts/:id/suggested-product`).

Decisions the user confirmed on 2026-10-06:
- Replaces issue 37's endpoint in place (`GET /store/carts/:id/suggested-product`), no separate route; issue 37 code was meant to be changed. Returns `null` when nothing in the cart's categories is eligible (catalog-wide fallback removed).
- Selection logic in a core-flows workflow/steps like issue 37, not a module service (module isolation: product module can't see orders).
- Only the categories directly on a product count (no parent/child expansion).
- Internal (`is_internal`) and inactive categories are skipped.
- In-category products that have never sold are eligible (fallback within the category, by creation date).

- Suggestions must be purchasable in the cart's region (user asked to fix issue 37's region bug class): besides price-in-cart-context, stock and sales channel, products requiring shipping need a store-enabled, priced shipping option for their shipping profile at a sales-channel location that serves the cart's shipping address, or any region country when there's no address yet. Calculated-price options count without a price; per-location stock (`insufficient_inventory`) isn't checked since checkout doesn't block on it.
- `StoreCartSuggestedProductResponse` TSDoc in packages/core/types/src/http/cart/store/responses.ts intentionally NOT updated (still mentions the catalog-wide fallback): any change under types/src/http triggers the full Validate HTTP Types CI job, which fails on 9 pre-existing product-option/notification type drifts on develop. User chose to avoid triggering it (2026-10-06).

Defaults I proposed that the user didn't object to:
- "Top-selling" = units sold over the most recent 1000 orders in the cart's sales channel (same as issue 37).
- Multiple categories: one pool across all cart categories, best seller wins, ties broken by product ID.
- Queried live, not cached.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 19:38:36Z)**_

The story is clear on the goal but not ready to implement. Its three "Open Questions" are the main design decisions, and several acceptance criteria could be read in more than one way. It is also much larger than the earlier issues (37, 38, 42). It would need a new module, payment changes, a scheduler, and both Admin and Store APIs.

## What I found in the codebase

- **No subscription support exists.** The only mention is a doc comment in [complete-cart.ts:79](packages/core/core-flows/src/cart/workflows/complete-cart.ts#L79). It links to Medusa's Subscriptions *recipe*, where subscriptions are a custom module in the user's own project, not part of core.
- **Recurring charges aren't built in.** Payment providers have no recurring-charge method. Off-session charging is still possible with what's there:
  - Customers can have "account holders" (stored customer records at the payment provider) through the `customer-account-holder` link.
  - Providers can optionally implement `savePaymentMethod` and `listPaymentMethods` ([provider.ts:658-703](packages/core/types/src/payment/provider.ts#L658-L703)).
  - Stripe already passes `off_session` and `payment_method` through to the payment intent ([stripe-base.ts:140-144](packages/modules/providers/payment-stripe/src/core/stripe-base.ts#L140-L144)).
  - Stripe is the only provider that can do this. The default system provider can't charge a saved method.
- **Scheduling is partly wired up.** The loader already reads jobs from `packages/medusa/src/jobs` ([loaders/index.ts:77](packages/medusa/src/loaders/index.ts#L77)), but that directory is empty. So a scheduled job is the natural place for the renewal loop.

## Questions to resolve before starting

**The ticket's own open questions (my recommendations):**
1. **New core module or plugin?** I recommend a new `packages/modules/subscription` module. It matches the repo structure and how this fork has added features so far.
2. **Who handles scheduling and retries?** I recommend Medusa does it: a scheduled job, plus off-session charges through the provider's saved payment method. Stripe's own Billing product would mean a provider-specific design.
3. **What happens on a price change or when a product is discontinued?** Pick one:
   - Lock the price at sign-up, or re-price at each renewal.
   - When a product is deleted or unpublished, either cancel the subscription or pause it as "ended".

**Ambiguities in the acceptance criteria:**

4. **Product or variant?** I'd attach eligibility to the variant, since price and inventory live there. Do we also need interval counts like "every 2 weeks", or only weekly/monthly/yearly?
5. **How does a customer buy a subscription with no storefront UI?** I'd add a subscription interval to the Store API "add line item" request.
   - "Alongside a one-time purchase" means a mixed cart. Can one cart hold both, with one subscription created per subscribed line item?
   - Must the customer be logged in? Saved payment methods require an account holder, so guest checkout probably can't work.
6. **What does a renewal order contain?**
   - Does it reuse the original shipping address and shipping method?
   - Are tax and shipping recalculated each time?
   - Do promotions from the first order carry over?
   - What happens if the variant is out of stock at renewal?
7. **What is the failed-payment policy?** For example: 3 retries spaced 1, 3 and 7 days apart, status `past_due`, then `canceled` after the last failure.
   - Stripe can also return `requires_action` (3D Secure). Should that count as a failure?
   - Should the customer be notified through the notification module?
8. **Cancellation:**
   - Does it take effect immediately or at the end of the current period?
   - Should store managers also see and cancel subscriptions through the Admin API?
   - "Otherwise ends": do we support a fixed number of cycles or an end date, or only cancellation and payment failure?
9. **Admin dashboard UI:** in or out? Only the storefront UI is explicitly out of scope.
10. **Size:** I'd suggest splitting this into at least two PRs:
    - Module, configuration and purchase.
    - Renewal job, payments and retries.

## Proposed plan and where it fits

**1. New module `packages/modules/subscription`**, following the `MedusaService` pattern:
- **Models:**
  - `SubscriptionPlan`: variant ID, allowed intervals, active flag.
  - `Subscription`: customer, variant, quantity, interval, status (`active` / `past_due` / `canceled` / `expired`), current period, `next_billing_at`, retry count, last failure, `canceled_at`, saved payment method reference, and shipping snapshot.
  - Optionally `SubscriptionCharge`: an attempt log, to make failures visible.
- **Registration:**
  - Add `Modules.SUBSCRIPTION` in utils.
  - Add types under `packages/core/types/src/subscription`.
  - Add the re-export in `packages/medusa/src/modules/`.

**2. Links** in [link-modules/src/definitions/](packages/modules/link-modules/src/definitions/): subscription↔customer, subscription↔order (one to many, one order per cycle), and plan↔product variant.

**3. Workflows** in `packages/core/core-flows/src/subscription/`:
- `create/update/deleteSubscriptionPlansWorkflow`
- `createSubscriptionsFromOrderWorkflow`: triggered on order placement for line items marked as subscriptions. It saves the payment method with `setup_future_usage: off_session`.
- `renewSubscriptionWorkflow`: creates the order (reusing the existing order and payment-collection steps), then authorizes and captures with `off_session` and the saved method. Compensation rolls back the order if payment fails, then records the failure and schedules the retry.
- `cancelSubscriptionWorkflow`
- Each workflow gets hooks.

**4. Scheduler:** a job in `packages/medusa/src/jobs/` (for example, hourly). It queries subscriptions that are due or due for a retry, then runs the renewal workflow for each one with a lock, so the same cycle can't be charged twice.

**5. API routes** in `packages/medusa/src/api/`:
- **Admin:** subscription plan CRUD (or nested under product variants), and subscriptions list, retrieve and cancel.
- **Store:** `/store/customers/me/subscriptions` list and retrieve, plus `POST .../:id/cancel`. Also a line-item validator extension to choose an interval.
- HTTP types go in `packages/core/types/src/http/subscription`. From the issue 38 work: any change there triggers the Validate HTTP Types CI job, which fails on drift that already exists on `develop`. That's unavoidable here, so we should plan for it.

**6. Tests:**
- Unit tests for interval and retry date math.
- Module integration tests.
- HTTP integration tests covering purchase, renewal (job invoked directly), failed payment with retry and status change, and cancellation.

**7. Changeset.**

Once you've answered these (especially 3, 5, 6 and 7), I can write the detailed plan. I'll also save the decisions to memory for the PR's design-decisions section, as we did for issue 38.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 20:23:10Z)**_

Mostly, yes. Your answers remove most of the complexity: no retries, no admin views of subscriptions, no proration or pausing, one PR. Two things still need a decision first.

**1. Does "just create a subscription" include automatic renewal?**
- If it means only creating the subscription record, it doesn't meet the acceptance criteria. Those require creating a new order and charging the customer each interval, and handling failed payments visibly.
- I'd keep renewal in, at its simplest: one scheduled job and one renewal workflow. Without it a subscription is just a record and nothing happens.

**2. Carrying promotions over to renewals works against "as simple as possible."**
- Renewals are repriced each cycle. The original promotion may have expired or run out of uses by then, so we'd need rules for checking it again.
- I'd drop this: renewals at the current price with no promotions. Is that OK?

**Two smaller points I'd settle this way unless you object:**
- **What happens on a failed renewal?** Payment failure and out-of-stock both mean no order and no shipment. From your answer 8, the subscription then ends with status `failed` and the reason recorded, so the failure is visible rather than silent. Should out-of-stock end it too, or just skip that cycle? Ending it is simpler.
- **Where subscriptions get created:** at checkout, not through a standalone "create subscription" endpoint. Checkout is where Stripe can save the card for later charges, and there's no Store API for listing saved payment methods yet. The customer adds a line item with a `subscription_interval`; when the order is placed, one subscription is created per such line item. The customer must be logged in.

## Simplified plan

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| `packages/modules/subscription` | Two models.<br>`SubscriptionPlan`: variant ID and allowed intervals (weekly/monthly/yearly).<br>`Subscription`: customer, variant, quantity, interval, status (`active` / `canceled` / `failed`), next billing date, saved payment method, original order ID, failure reason. |
| Links | subscription↔customer, subscription↔order (each renewal order is linked) |
| Workflows (core-flows) | Plan create/update/delete.<br>`createSubscriptionsFromOrder`: runs when an order is placed.<br>`renewSubscription`: builds a cart from the original order's address and shipping method so tax, shipping and price are recalculated. It then completes the cart with the saved card off-session. On any failure, no order is created and the subscription is marked `failed`.<br>`cancelSubscription` |
| Job | `packages/medusa/src/jobs/renew-subscriptions.ts`: hourly, runs the renewal for subscriptions that are due |
| Admin API | Plan configuration for a variant. That's all for admin. |
| Store API | `subscription_interval` on add line item.<br>`GET /store/customers/me/subscriptions` (list and retrieve).<br>`POST /store/customers/me/subscriptions/:id/cancel`: cancels immediately. |
| Tests | Module integration tests.<br>HTTP integration tests: purchase creates a subscription, renewal creates an order, failure sets `failed`, cancel. |

Renewal relies on Stripe's saved payment methods. With the default system provider, renewals will always fail, and integration tests will need a mocked provider.

Once you've answered 1 and 2, I'll save these decisions to memory for the PR description and write the detailed plan.

```markdown
Subscriptions story (source: Medusa discussions #2942). User wants everything as simple as possible, one PR.

Decisions the user confirmed on 2026-10-06:
- New core module `packages/modules/subscription` (not a plugin).
- Medusa does its own scheduling (scheduled job) and charges the saved payment method off-session; no provider-native billing.
- Renewals are repriced at renewal time (current price, tax, shipping recalculated); no promotions carried over.
- Eligibility is per variant; intervals limited to weekly/monthly/yearly (no interval counts).
- Purchase happens at checkout via the Store API only: line item carries a `subscription_interval`; mixed carts allowed; one subscription per subscribed line item; customer must be logged in.
- Renewal reuses the original order's shipping address and shipping method by default.
- Renewal in scope. Any renewal failure (payment failure or out of stock) = no order/shipment, no retries, subscription ends with status `failed` and recorded reason.
- Customer cancel is immediate. No admin view/cancel of subscriptions (admin only configures plans on variants). Subscriptions end only by cancel or failure (no end dates/cycle counts).
- Admin dashboard UI and storefront UI out of scope.

**Why:** The user writes a "Design decisions" section in PR descriptions (same as [[issue-38-design-decisions]]).
**How to apply:** Build the plan/PR within these limits; list these decisions with reasoning in the PR.
```

```text
     5	} from "@medusajs/framework/types"

     7	  Modules,

     9	  PaymentWebhookEvents,
    10	} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
    11	import { SubscriberArgs, SubscriberConfig } from "../types/subscribers"
    12	
    13	type SerializedBuffer = {
    14	  data: ArrayBuffer
    15	  type: "Buffer"
    16	}
    17	
    18	export default async function paymentWebhookhandler({
    19	  event,
    20	  container,
    21	}: SubscriberArgs<ProviderWebhookPayload>) {
    22	  const paymentService: IPaymentModuleService = container.resolve(
    23	    Modules.PAYMENT
    24	  )
    25	
    26	  const input = event.data
    27	
    28	  if (
    29	    (input.payload?.rawData as unknown as SerializedBuffer)?.type === "Buffer"
    30	  ) {
    31	    input.payload.rawData = Buffer.from(
    32	      (input.payload.rawData as unknown as SerializedBuffer).data
    33	    )
    34	  }
    35	
    36	  const processedEvent = await paymentService.getWebhookActionAndData(input)
    37	
    38	  // Without a payment session id we cannot associate the event with a specific
    39	  // payment session (and therefore cart). Processing it would let the workflow
    40	  // resolve to an arbitrary, unrelated payment session/cart, so we ignore it.
    41	  // This guards against e.g. foreign events delivered by a provider account
    42	  // shared with another integration.
    43	  if (!processedEvent.data?.session_id) {
    44	    return
    45	  }
    46	
    47	  if (
    48	    processedEvent?.action === PaymentActions.NOT_SUPPORTED ||
    49	    // We currently don't handle these payment statuses in the processPayment function.
    50	    processedEvent?.action === PaymentActions.CANCELED ||
    51	    processedEvent?.action === PaymentActions.FAILED ||
    52	    processedEvent?.action === PaymentActions.REQUIRES_MORE ||
    53	    processedEvent?.action === PaymentActions.PENDING_AUTHORIZATION
    54	  ) {
    55	    return
    56	  }
    57	
    58	  const wfEngine = container.resolve(Modules.WORKFLOW_ENGINE)
    59	  await wfEngine.run(processPaymentWorkflowId, { input: processedEvent })
    60	}
```

```text
index.ts

payment-provider.ts
    input: GetPaymentStatusInput
  ): Promise<GetPaymentStatusOutput> {
    const id = input?.data?.id as string
    if (!id) {
      throw this.buildError(
        "No payment intent ID provided while getting payment status",
        new Error("No payment intent ID provided")
      )
    }

    const paymentIntent = await this.stripe_.paymentIntents.retrieve(id, {
      expand: ["payment_method"],
    })
    const statusResponse = this.getStatus(paymentIntent)

    return statusResponse as unknown as GetPaymentStatusOutput
  }

  async initiatePayment({
    currency_code,
    amount,
    data,
    context,
  }: InitiatePaymentInput): Promise<InitiatePaymentOutput> {
    const additionalParameters = this.normalizePaymentIntentParameters(data)

    const intentRequest: Stripe.PaymentIntentCreateParams = {
      amount: getSmallestUnit(amount, currency_code),
      currency: currency_code,
      metadata: {
        ...(data?.metadata ?? {}),
        session_id: data?.session_id as string,
      },
      ...additionalParameters,
      expand: ["payment_method"],
    }

    intentRequest.customer = context?.account_holder?.data?.id as
      | string
      | undefined

    const sessionData = await this.executeWithRetry<Stripe.PaymentIntent>(() =>
      this.stripe_.paymentIntents.create(intentRequest, {
        idempotencyKey: context?.idempotency_key,
      })
    )
    const isPaymentIntent = "id" in sessionData
    return {
      id: isPaymentIntent ? sessionData.id : (data?.session_id as string),
      ...(this.getStatus(
        sessionData as unknown as Stripe.PaymentIntent
      ) as unknown as Pick<InitiatePaymentOutput, "data" | "status">),
    }
  }

  async authorizePayment(
    input: AuthorizePaymentInput
  ): Promise<AuthorizePaymentOutput> {
    return this.getPaymentStatus(input)
  }

  async cancelPayment({
    data,
    context,
  }: CancelPaymentInput): Promise<CancelPaymentOutput> {
    try {
      const id = data?.id as string

      if (!id) {
        return { data: data }
      }

      const res = await this.stripe_.paymentIntents.cancel(id, {
        idempotencyKey: context?.idempotency_key,
      })
      return { data: res as unknown as Record<string, unknown> }
    } catch (error) {
      if (error.payment_intent?.status === ErrorIntentStatus.CANCELED) {
        return { data: error.payment_intent }
      }

      throw this.buildError("An error occurred in cancelPayment", error)
    }
  }

  async capturePayment({
    data,
    context,
  }: CapturePaymentInput): Promise<CapturePaymentOutput> {
    const id = data?.id as string

    try {
      const intent = await this.stripe_.paymentIntents.capture(id, {
        idempotencyKey: context?.idempotency_key,
      })
      return { data: intent as unknown as Record<string, unknown> }
    } catch (error) {
      if (error.code === ErrorCodes.PAYMENT_INTENT_UNEXPECTED_STATE) {
        if (error.payment_intent?.status === ErrorIntentStatus.SUCCEEDED) {
          return { data: error.payment_intent }
        }
  normalizePaymentIntentParameters(
    extra?: Record<string, unknown>
  ): Partial<Stripe.PaymentIntentCreateParams> {
    const res = {} as Partial<Stripe.PaymentIntentCreateParams>

    res.description = (extra?.payment_description ??
      this.options_?.paymentDescription) as string

    res.capture_method =
      (extra?.capture_method as "automatic" | "manual") ??
      this.paymentIntentOptions.capture_method ??
      (this.options_.capture ? "automatic" : "manual")

    res.setup_future_usage =
      (extra?.setup_future_usage as "off_session" | "on_session" | undefined) ??
      this.paymentIntentOptions.setup_future_usage

    res.payment_method_types =
      (extra?.payment_method_types as string[]) ??
      (this.paymentIntentOptions.payment_method_types as string[])

    res.payment_method_data =
      extra?.payment_method_data as Stripe.PaymentIntentCreateParams.PaymentMethodData

    res.payment_method_options =
      (extra?.payment_method_options as Stripe.PaymentIntentCreateParams.PaymentMethodOptions) ??
      this.paymentIntentOptions.payment_method_options

    res.automatic_payment_methods =
      (extra?.automatic_payment_methods as { enabled: true } | undefined) ??
      (this.options_?.automaticPaymentMethods ? { enabled: true } : undefined)

    res.off_session = extra?.off_session as boolean | undefined

    res.confirm = extra?.confirm as boolean | undefined

    res.payment_method = extra?.payment_method as string | undefined

    res.return_url = extra?.return_url as string | undefined
```

```text
  private getStatus(paymentIntent: Stripe.PaymentIntent): {
    data: Stripe.PaymentIntent
    status: PaymentSessionStatus
  } {
    switch (paymentIntent.status) {
      case "requires_payment_method":
        if (paymentIntent.last_payment_error) {
          return { status: PaymentSessionStatus.ERROR, data: paymentIntent }
        }
        return { status: PaymentSessionStatus.PENDING, data: paymentIntent }
      case "requires_confirmation":
        return { status: PaymentSessionStatus.PENDING, data: paymentIntent }
      case "processing":
        if (
          this.isAsyncPaymentMethod(
            paymentIntent.payment_method as Stripe.PaymentMethod
          )
        ) {
          return {
            status: PaymentSessionStatus.PENDING_AUTHORIZATION,
            data: paymentIntent,
          }
        }
        return { status: PaymentSessionStatus.PENDING, data: paymentIntent }
      case "requires_action":
        return {
          status: PaymentSessionStatus.REQUIRES_MORE,
          data: paymentIntent,
        }
      case "canceled":
        return { status: PaymentSessionStatus.CANCELED, data: paymentIntent }
      case "requires_capture":
        return { status: PaymentSessionStatus.AUTHORIZED, data: paymentIntent }
      case "succeeded":
        return { status: PaymentSessionStatus.CAPTURED, data: paymentIntent }
      default:
        return { status: PaymentSessionStatus.PENDING, data: paymentIntent }
    }
  }
```

```text
  async createPaymentSession(
    paymentCollectionId: string,
    input: CreatePaymentSessionDTO,
    @MedusaContext() sharedContext?: Context
  ): Promise<PaymentSessionDTO> {
    let paymentSession: InferEntityType<typeof PaymentSession> | undefined
    let providerPaymentSession: InitiatePaymentOutput | undefined

    try {
      paymentSession = await this.createPaymentSession_(
        paymentCollectionId,
        input,
        sharedContext
      )

      providerPaymentSession = await this.paymentProviderService_.createSession(
        input.provider_id,
        {
          context: {
            idempotency_key: paymentSession!.id,
            ...input.context,
          },
          data: { ...input.data, session_id: paymentSession!.id },
          amount: input.amount,
          currency_code: normalizeCurrencyCode(input.currency_code),
        }
      )

      paymentSession = await this.paymentSessionService_.update(
        {
          id: paymentSession!.id,
          data: { ...input.data, ...providerPaymentSession.data },
          status: providerPaymentSession.status ?? PaymentSessionStatus.PENDING,
        },
        sharedContext
      )
    } catch (error) {
      if (providerPaymentSession) {
        await this.paymentProviderService_.deleteSession(input.provider_id, {
          data: input.data,
        })
      }
  async authorizePaymentSession(
    id: string,
    context: Record<string, unknown>,
    @MedusaContext() sharedContext?: Context
  ): Promise<PaymentDTO | null> {
    const session = await this.paymentSessionService_.retrieve(
      id,
      {
        select: [
          "id",
          "data",
          "provider_id",
          "amount",
          "raw_amount",
          "currency_code",
          "authorized_at",
          "payment_collection_id",
        ],
        relations: ["payment", "payment_collection"],
      },
      sharedContext
    )

    // this method needs to be idempotent
    if (session.payment && session.authorized_at) {
      return await this.baseRepository_.serialize<PaymentDTO>(session.payment)
    }

    let { data, status } = await this.paymentProviderService_.authorizePayment(
      session.provider_id,
      {
        data: session.data,
        context: { idempotency_key: session.id, ...context },
      }
    )

    if (status === PaymentSessionStatus.PENDING_AUTHORIZATION) {
      await this.paymentSessionService_.update(
        {
          id: session.id,
          status,
          data,
        },
        sharedContext
      )

      await this.maybeUpdatePaymentCollection_(
        session.payment_collection_id,
        sharedContext
      )

      return null
    }

    if (
      status !== PaymentSessionStatus.AUTHORIZED &&
      status !== PaymentSessionStatus.CAPTURED
    ) {
      await this.paymentSessionService_.update(
        {
          id: session.id,
          status,
          data,
        },
        sharedContext
      )
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
        `Session: ${session.id} was not authorized with the provider.`
      )
    }

    let payment
    try {
      payment = await this.authorizePaymentSession_(
        session,
        data,
        status as PaymentSessionStatus,
        sharedContext
      )
    } catch (error) {
      await this.paymentProviderService_.cancelPayment(session.provider_id, {
        data,
        context: {
          idempotency_key: payment?.id,
          ...context,
        },
      })

      throw error
    }

    await this.maybeUpdatePaymentCollection_(
      session.payment_collection_id,
      sharedContext
    )

    return await this.baseRepository_.serialize<PaymentDTO>(payment)
  }

  @InjectTransactionManager()
  protected async authorizePaymentSession_(
    session: InferEntityType<typeof PaymentSession>,
    data: Record<string, unknown> | undefined,
    status: PaymentSessionStatus,
    @MedusaContext() sharedContext?: Context
  ): Promise<InferEntityType<typeof Payment>> {
    let isCaptured = false
    if (status === PaymentSessionStatus.CAPTURED) {
      status = PaymentSessionStatus.AUTHORIZED
      isCaptured = true
    }

    await this.paymentSessionService_.update(
      {
        id: session.id,
        data,
        status,
        ...(session.authorized_at === null
          ? {
              authorized_at: new Date(),
            }
          : {}),
      },
      sharedContext
    )

        provider_id: session.provider_id,
        data,
      },
```

```text
export const reserveInventoryStep = createStep(
  reserveInventoryStepId,
  async (data: ReserveVariantInventoryStepInput, { container }) => {
    if (!data.items.length) {
      return new StepResponse([], {
        reservations: [],
        inventoryItemIds: [],
      })
    }

    const inventoryService = container.resolve(Modules.INVENTORY)
    const locking = container.resolve(Modules.LOCKING)

    const inventoryItemIds: string[] = []

    const items = data.items.map((item) => {
      inventoryItemIds.push(item.inventory_item_id)

      return {
        line_item_id: item.id,
        inventory_item_id: item.inventory_item_id,
        quantity: MathBN.mult(item.required_quantity, item.quantity),
        allow_backorder: item.allow_backorder,
        location_id: item.location_ids[0],
      }
    })

    const lockingKeys = Array.from(new Set(inventoryItemIds))

    const reservations = await locking.execute(lockingKeys, async () => {
      return await inventoryService.createReservationItems(items)
    })

    return new StepResponse(reservations, {
      reservations: reservations.map((r) => r.id),
      inventoryItemIds,
```

```text
export async function zodValidator<T>(
  zodSchema: z.ZodObject<any, any> | z.ZodType<any, any, any>,
  body: T
): Promise<z.output<z.ZodObject<any, any> | z.ZodType<any, any, any>>> {
  let strictSchema = zodSchema
  if ("strict" in zodSchema) {
    strictSchema = zodSchema.strict()
  }

  try {
    return await strictSchema.parseAsync(body)
  } catch (err) {
    if (isZodError(err)) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
        `Invalid request: ${formatError(err, body)}`
}

import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<
    HttpTypes.AdminCreateVariantInventoryItem,
    HttpTypes.SelectParams
  >,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminProductVariantResponse>
) => {
  const variantId = req.params.variant_id

  await createLinksWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: [
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 20:38:22Z)**_

Both research reports are back. The decisions hold up against the code, and the plan is below. The research changed three things from my earlier outline:

- **The checkout event fires too early.** The order-placed event is emitted before payment is authorized. Subscriptions will be created by a step inside checkout itself, after payment succeeds, instead of by listening for that event.
- **The add-line-item request rejects unknown fields** (its validator is strict). So I'll add `subscription_interval` to that validator directly.
- **Correction:** I said earlier that renewals would always fail with the default system payment provider. That's wrong. The system provider approves every payment, so renewals "succeed" without charging anything. That's useful for integration tests, but it means only Stripe actually charges a saved card.

## Plan

**1. Module: `packages/modules/subscription`** (copied from the `api-key` module's layout)
- **Models:**
  - `SubscriptionPlan`: `variant_id` (unique), `intervals` (array of `weekly` / `monthly` / `yearly`).
  - `Subscription`: `customer_id`, `variant_id`, `quantity`, `interval`, `status` (`active` / `canceled` / `failed`), `next_billing_at`, `canceled_at`, `failed_at`, `failure_reason`, `payment_provider_id`, `payment_method_id`.
- `SubscriptionModuleService` extends `MedusaService`, plus a small helper that calculates the next billing date (month-end dates are clamped, so Jan 31 becomes Feb 28).
- Initial migration generated with `yarn migration:initial`.

**2. Registration**
- Add `Modules.SUBSCRIPTION` and its package name in [definition.ts](packages/core/utils/src/modules-sdk/definition.ts).
- Add an entry in [modules-sdk definitions.ts](packages/core/modules-sdk/src/definitions.ts).
- Enable it by default in [define-config.ts](packages/core/utils/src/common/define-config.ts), with no feature flag. This means updating the inline snapshots in `define-config.spec.ts`.
- Add types in `packages/core/types/src/subscription/` and export them from the types package entry files.
- Add the service type to [container.ts](packages/core/framework/src/types/container.ts).
- Add `packages/medusa/src/modules/subscription.ts`, the dependency in the medusa `package.json`, and an entry in `.eslintignore`.

**3. Links** in [link-modules/src/definitions/](packages/modules/link-modules/src/definitions/)
- `order-subscription`: a real link table, one subscription to many orders. The first order and every renewal order are linked here. This is what ties subscriptions to orders.
- Read-only links (no extra tables) from subscription to customer and from plan to product variant, so subscriptions and plans can be fetched together with that data.

**4. Purchase at checkout**
- **Add to cart:** `StoreAddCartLineItem` in [validators.ts](packages/medusa/src/api/store/carts/validators.ts) gets an optional `subscription_interval`. The route stores it as `metadata.subscription_interval` on the line item. Checkout already copies line-item metadata onto the order line items.
- **Validation:** a new `validateSubscriptionItemsStep` checks that the variant has a plan offering that interval. It runs in `addToCartWorkflow`, so the request fails early. At checkout it runs again and also requires the cart to have a logged-in customer.
- **Creating subscriptions:** a new `createSubscriptionsFromOrderStep` runs inside `completeCartWorkflow` after payment is authorized. It creates one subscription per subscribed line item and links each to the order. It reads the saved card's ID from the authorized payment (`data.payment_method.id` for Stripe).

**5. Workflows** in `packages/core/core-flows/src/subscription/`
- `upsertSubscriptionPlanWorkflow` and `deleteSubscriptionPlanWorkflow`.
- `cancelSubscriptionWorkflow`: checks that the subscription belongs to the customer and is still `active`, then sets `canceled`.
- `renewSubscriptionWorkflow`:
  1. Lock the subscription and re-check that it's still due.
  2. Load the original order.
  3. Create a cart with the same region, sales channel, customer, email and shipping address.
  4. Add the variant at its current price.
  5. Add the original shipping option.
  6. Create a payment collection and a payment session with `{ payment_method, off_session: true, confirm: true }`.
  7. Complete the cart.
  8. Link the new order to the subscription and advance `next_billing_at`.

  Steps 3 to 7 reuse the existing cart workflows, so tax, shipping and inventory are recalculated by the same code as a normal checkout.
- `failSubscriptionWorkflow`: sets `failed`, `failed_at` and `failure_reason`. If renewal throws anywhere (declined payment, out of stock, shipping option no longer available), the existing compensation steps roll back the cart and order. The job then runs this workflow. No retries.

**6. Scheduled job: `packages/medusa/src/jobs/renew-subscriptions.ts`**
- Runs hourly.
- Lists active subscriptions with `next_billing_at <= now`, in batches.
- Runs the renewal for each one, and on error runs `failSubscriptionWorkflow`.

**7. API routes**
- **Admin:** `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE` on `/admin/products/:id/variants/:variant_id/subscription-plan`, placed next to `inventory-items` with the same middleware and permission pattern.
- **Store:**
  - `GET /store/customers/me/subscriptions` and `GET .../:id`.
  - `POST .../:id/cancel`.
  - The existing `/store/customers/me*` login middleware already covers these routes.
- **HTTP types:** go in `packages/core/types/src/http/subscription/`. As with issue 38, this will trigger the Validate HTTP Types CI job, which fails on existing drift on `develop`. A new resource can't avoid it this time.

**8. Tests**
- Unit tests for the next-billing-date helper.
- Module integration tests for the service.
- HTTP integration tests using the system provider and running the job handler directly:
  - Plan configuration.
  - Rejecting an interval the plan doesn't offer, and rejecting a guest checkout.
  - Checkout creating subscriptions.
  - Renewal creating a linked order and advancing the billing date.
  - Out of stock leading to `failed` with no new order.
  - Cancellation, including that a canceled subscription isn't renewed.
- A real declined card can only be tested against Stripe. That path is the same compensation-then-`failed` code as out-of-stock, so I'll cover it with a step-level test that forces the payment to fail.

**9. Docs and changeset:** TSDoc on the new types and workflows, and one changeset.

## One decision left

For Stripe to save the card for later charges, the payment session must be created with `setup_future_usage: "off_session"`. Two ways to handle it:

- **Client sends it (my recommendation):** the client includes it in the payment session `data` it already sends, and we document that. If a subscribed order's authorized payment has no saved card, checkout fails, so it never fails silently.
- **We set it automatically:** we detect subscription items in the cart when the payment session is created. That means changing the payment-collection workflow, which doesn't know about carts today.

Once you choose, I can start implementing. If you prefer, I can write this plan into `thoughts/shared/plans/` first.

```bash
/**
 * @enum
 *
 * The interval at which a subscription renews.
 */
export enum SubscriptionInterval {
  /**
   * The subscription renews every week.
   */
  WEEKLY = "weekly",
  /**
   * The subscription renews every month.
   */
  MONTHLY = "monthly",
  /**
   * The subscription renews every year.
   */
  YEARLY = "yearly",
}

/**
 * @enum
 *
 * The status of a subscription.
 */
export enum SubscriptionStatus {
  /**
   * The subscription renews at its next billing date.
   */
  ACTIVE = "active",
  /**
   * The customer canceled the subscription.
   */
  CANCELED = "canceled",
  /**
   * A renewal failed, for example because the payment was declined or the
   * variant was out of stock, which ended the subscription.
   */
  FAILED = "failed",
}

/**
 * The key of the line item metadata that holds the subscription interval
 * a customer chose for the item.
 */
export const SUBSCRIPTION_INTERVAL_METADATA_KEY = "subscription_interval"

/**
 * Computes the date a subscription is next billed, one interval after the
 * given date. When the target month is shorter than the source day (for
 * example, monthly from January 31), the date is clamped to the last day of
 * the target month.
 *
 * @param from - The date to compute from.
 * @param interval - The subscription's interval.
 * @returns The next billing date.
 */
export function computeNextBillingDate(
  from: Date,
  interval: SubscriptionInterval | `${SubscriptionInterval}`
): Date {
  const next = new Date(from.getTime())

  if (interval === SubscriptionInterval.WEEKLY) {
    next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 7)
    return next
  }

  const monthsToAdd = interval === SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY ? 1 : 12
  const day = next.getUTCDate()

  next.setUTCDate(1)
  next.setUTCMonth(next.getUTCMonth() + monthsToAdd)

  const lastDayOfTargetMonth = new Date(
    Date.UTC(next.getUTCFullYear(), next.getUTCMonth() + 1, 0)
  ).getUTCDate()

  next.setUTCDate(Math.min(day, lastDayOfTargetMonth))

  return next
}
EOF

cat > __tests__/compute-next-billing-date.spec.ts <<'EOF'
import { computeNextBillingDate, SubscriptionInterval } from "../subscription"

describe("computeNextBillingDate", () => {
  it("adds seven days for a weekly interval", () => {
    const next = computeNextBillingDate(
      new Date("2026-12-29T10:00:00.000Z"),
      SubscriptionInterval.WEEKLY
    )

    expect(next.toISOString()).toEqual("2027-01-05T10:00:00.000Z")
  })

  it("adds one month for a monthly interval", () => {
    const next = computeNextBillingDate(
      new Date("2026-03-15T10:00:00.000Z"),
      SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY
    )

    expect(next.toISOString()).toEqual("2026-04-15T10:00:00.000Z")
  })

  it("clamps a monthly interval to the end of a shorter month", () => {
    const next = computeNextBillingDate(
      new Date("2026-01-31T10:00:00.000Z"),
      SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY
    )

    expect(next.toISOString()).toEqual("2026-02-28T10:00:00.000Z")
  })

  it("rolls a monthly interval over to the next year", () => {
    const next = computeNextBillingDate(
      new Date("2026-12-31T10:00:00.000Z"),
      SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY
    )

    expect(next.toISOString()).toEqual("2027-01-31T10:00:00.000Z")
  })

  it("adds one year for a yearly interval", () => {
    const next = computeNextBillingDate(
      new Date("2026-06-01T10:00:00.000Z"),
      SubscriptionInterval.YEARLY
    )

    expect(next.toISOString()).toEqual("2027-06-01T10:00:00.000Z")
  })

  it("clamps a yearly interval from a leap day", () => {
    const next = computeNextBillingDate(
      new Date("2028-02-29T10:00:00.000Z"),
      SubscriptionInterval.YEARLY
    )

    expect(next.toISOString()).toEqual("2029-02-28T10:00:00.000Z")
  })

  it("does not mutate the input date", () => {
    const from = new Date("2026-03-15T10:00:00.000Z")

    computeNextBillingDate(from, SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY)

    expect(from.toISOString()).toEqual("2026-03-15T10:00:00.000Z")
  })
})
EOF
```

export interface FilterableTranslationProps
  extends BaseFilterable<FilterableTranslationProps> {
  /**
   * Search through translated content using this search term.
   * This searches within the JSONB translations field values.
   */
  q?: string

  /**
   * The IDs to filter the translations by.
   */
  id?: string[] | string | OperatorMap<string | string[]>

  /**
   * Filter translations by entity ID.
   */
  reference_id?: string | string[] | OperatorMap<string>

  /**
   * Filter translations by entity type.
   */
  reference?: string | string[] | OperatorMap<string>

  /**
   * Filter translations by locale code.
   */
  locale_code?: string | string[] | OperatorMap<string>
}
 * Method signatures match what MedusaService generates.
 */
export interface ITranslationModuleService extends IModuleService {
  /**
   * This method retrieves a locale by its ID.
   *
   * @param {string} id - The ID of the locale.
   * @param {FindConfig<LocaleDTO>} config - The configurations determining how the locale is retrieved. Its properties, such as `select` or `relations`, accept the
   * attributes or relations associated with a locale.
   * @param {Context} sharedContext - A context used to share resources, such as transaction manager, between the application and the module.
   * @returns {Promise<LocaleDTO>} The retrieved locale.
   *
   * @example
   * A simple example that retrieves a locale by its ID:
   *
   * ```ts
   * const locale = await translationModuleService.retrieveLocale("loc_123")
   * ```
   *
   * To specify relations that should be retrieved:
   *
   * :::note
   *
   * You can only retrieve data models defined in the same module. To retrieve linked data models
   * from other modules, use [Query](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/module-links/query) instead.
   *
   * :::
   *
   * ```ts
   * const locale = await translationModuleService.retrieveLocale("loc_123", {
   *   relations: ["translations"],
   * })
   * ```
   */
  retrieveLocale(
    id: string,
    config?: FindConfig<LocaleDTO>,
    sharedContext?: Context
  ): Promise<LocaleDTO>

  /**
   * This method retrieves a paginated list of locales based on optional filters and configuration.
   *
   * @param {FilterableLocaleProps} filters - The filters to apply on the retrieved locales.
   * @param {FindConfig<LocaleDTO>} config - The configurations determining how the locale is retrieved. Its properties, such as `select` or `relations`, accept the
   * attributes or relations associated with a locale.
   * @param {Context} sharedContext - A context used to share resources, such as transaction manager, between the application and the module.
   * @returns {Promise<LocaleDTO[]>} The list of locales.
   *
   * @example
   * To retrieve a list of locales using their IDs:
   *
   * ```ts
   * const locales = await translationModuleService.listLocales({
   *   id: ["loc_123", "loc_321"],
   * })
   * ```
   *
   * To specify relations that should be retrieved within the locales:
   *
   * :::note
   *
   * You can only retrieve data models defined in the same module. To retrieve linked data models
   * from other modules, use [Query](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/module-links/query) instead.
   *
   * :::
   *
   * ```ts
   * const locales = await translationModuleService.listLocales(
   *   {
   *     id: ["loc_123", "loc_321"],
   *   },
   *   {
   *     relations: ["translations"],
   *   }
   * )
   * ```
   *
   * By default, only the first `15` records are retrieved. You can control pagination by specifying the `skip` and `take` properties of the `config` parameter:
   *
   * ```ts
   * const locales = await translationModuleService.listLocales(
   *   {
   *     id: ["loc_123", "loc_321"],
   *   },
   *   {
   *     relations: ["translations"],
   *     take: 20,
   *     skip: 2,
   *   }
   * )
   * ```
   */
  listLocales(
    filters?: FilterableLocaleProps,
    config?: FindConfig<LocaleDTO>,
    sharedContext?: Context
  ): Promise<LocaleDTO[]>

```bash
import { BaseFilterable, OperatorMap } from "../dal"

/**
 * The interval at which a subscription renews.
 */
export type SubscriptionIntervalType = "weekly" | "monthly" | "yearly"

/**
 * The status of a subscription.
 *
 * - `active`: The subscription renews at its next billing date.
 * - `canceled`: The customer canceled the subscription.
 * - `failed`: A renewal failed, which ended the subscription.
 */
export type SubscriptionStatusType = "active" | "canceled" | "failed"

/**
 * The subscription plan details. A subscription plan makes a product variant
 * available for purchase as a subscription.
 */
export interface SubscriptionPlanDTO {
  /**
   * The ID of the subscription plan.
   */
  id: string

  /**
   * The ID of the product variant the plan belongs to.
   */
  variant_id: string

  /**
   * The intervals a customer can subscribe to the variant at.
   */
  intervals: SubscriptionIntervalType[]

  /**
   * The date and time the subscription plan was created.
   */
  created_at: Date | string

  /**
   * The date and time the subscription plan was last updated.
   */
  updated_at: Date | string

  /**
   * The date and time the subscription plan was deleted.
   */
  deleted_at: Date | string | null
}

/**
 * The subscription details. A subscription renews a customer's purchase of a
 * product variant at a recurring interval.
 */
export interface SubscriptionDTO {
  /**
   * The ID of the subscription.
   */
  id: string

  /**
   * The ID of the customer the subscription belongs to.
   */
  customer_id: string

  /**
   * The ID of the product variant the customer subscribed to.
   */
  variant_id: string

  /**
   * The quantity of the variant ordered at each renewal.
   */
  quantity: number

  /**
   * The interval at which the subscription renews.
   */
  interval: SubscriptionIntervalType

  /**
   * The status of the subscription.
   */
  status: SubscriptionStatusType

  /**
   * The date and time the subscription is next renewed.
   */
  next_billing_at: Date | string

  /**
   * The ID of the payment provider used to charge renewals.
   */
  payment_provider_id: string

  /**
   * The ID of the saved payment method in the payment provider used to charge
   * renewals, if the provider returned one.
   */
  payment_method_id: string | null

  /**
   * The date and time the subscription was canceled.
   */
  canceled_at: Date | string | null

  /**
   * The date and time a renewal of the subscription failed.
   */
  failed_at: Date | string | null

  /**
   * The reason a renewal of the subscription failed.
   */
  failure_reason: string | null

  /**
   * The date and time the subscription was created.
   */
  created_at: Date | string

  /**
   * The date and time the subscription was last updated.
   */
  updated_at: Date | string

  /**
   * The date and time the subscription was deleted.
   */
  deleted_at: Date | string | null
}

/**
 * The filters to apply on the retrieved subscription plans.
 */
export interface FilterableSubscriptionPlanProps
  extends BaseFilterable<FilterableSubscriptionPlanProps> {
  /**
   * The IDs to filter the subscription plans by.
   */
  id?: string | string[] | OperatorMap<string | string[]>

  /**
   * The product variant IDs to filter the subscription plans by.
   */
  variant_id?: string | string[] | OperatorMap<string | string[]>
}

/**
 * The filters to apply on the retrieved subscriptions.
 */
export interface FilterableSubscriptionProps
  extends BaseFilterable<FilterableSubscriptionProps> {
  /**
   * The IDs to filter the subscriptions by.
   */
  id?: string | string[] | OperatorMap<string | string[]>

  /**
   * The customer IDs to filter the subscriptions by.
   */
  customer_id?: string | string[] | OperatorMap<string | string[]>

  /**
   * The product variant IDs to filter the subscriptions by.
   */
  variant_id?: string | string[] | OperatorMap<string | string[]>

  /**
   * The statuses to filter the subscriptions by.
   */
  status?:
    | SubscriptionStatusType
    | SubscriptionStatusType[]
    | OperatorMap<SubscriptionStatusType | SubscriptionStatusType[]>

  /**
   * Filter the subscriptions by their next billing date.
   */
  next_billing_at?: OperatorMap<string | Date>
}
```

```bash
    id: model.id({ prefix: "sub" }).primaryKey(),
    customer_id: model.text(),
    variant_id: model.text(),
    quantity: model.number(),
    interval: model.enum(SubscriptionInterval),
    status: model.enum(SubscriptionStatus).default(SubscriptionStatus.ACTIVE),
    next_billing_at: model.dateTime(),

    canceled_at: model.dateTime().nullable(),
    failed_at: model.dateTime().nullable(),

      where: "deleted_at IS NULL",

      on: ["status", "next_billing_at"],
      where: "deleted_at IS NULL",
    },
  ])

export default Subscription
```

```bash
cd /workspaces/medusa/packages/modules/subscription; cat > integration-tests/__tests__/subscription-module-service.spec.ts <<'EOF'
import { ISubscriptionModuleService } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  Module,
  Modules,
  SubscriptionInterval,
  SubscriptionStatus,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { moduleIntegrationTestRunner } from "@medusajs/test-utils"
import { SubscriptionModuleService } from "@services"

jest.setTimeout(100000)

moduleIntegrationTestRunner<ISubscriptionModuleService>({
  moduleName: Modules.SUBSCRIPTION,
  testSuite: ({ service }) => {
    it("should export the appropriate linkable configuration", () => {
      const linkable = Module(Modules.SUBSCRIPTION, {
        service: SubscriptionModuleService,
      }).linkable

      expect(Object.keys(linkable)).toEqual(
        expect.arrayContaining(["subscription", "subscriptionPlan"])
      )
    })

    describe("Subscription plans", () => {
      it("should create a plan with its intervals", async () => {
        const plan = await service.createSubscriptionPlans({
          variant_id: "variant_1",
          intervals: [SubscriptionInterval.WEEKLY, SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY],
        })

        expect(plan).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            id: expect.stringMatching(/^subplan_/),
            variant_id: "variant_1",
            intervals: ["weekly", "monthly"],
          })
        )
      })

      it("should allow only one plan per variant", async () => {
        await service.createSubscriptionPlans({
          variant_id: "variant_1",
          intervals: [SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY],
        })

        const error = await service
          .createSubscriptionPlans({
            variant_id: "variant_1",
            intervals: [SubscriptionInterval.YEARLY],
          })
          .catch((e) => e)

        expect(error.message).toContain("already exists")
      })

      it("should allow a new plan for a variant once the old one is deleted", async () => {
        const plan = await service.createSubscriptionPlans({
          variant_id: "variant_1",
          intervals: [SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY],
        })
        await service.softDeleteSubscriptionPlans([plan.id])

        const newPlan = await service.createSubscriptionPlans({
          variant_id: "variant_1",
          intervals: [SubscriptionInterval.YEARLY],
        })

        expect(newPlan.intervals).toEqual(["yearly"])
      })
    })

    describe("Subscriptions", () => {
      const subscriptionData = {
        customer_id: "cus_1",
        variant_id: "variant_1",
        quantity: 2,
        interval: SubscriptionInterval.MONTHLY,
        next_billing_at: new Date("2026-11-06T00:00:00.000Z"),
        payment_provider_id: "pp_stripe_stripe",
        payment_method_id: "pm_123",
      }

      it("should create an active subscription by default", async () => {
        const subscription = await service.createSubscriptions(subscriptionData)

        expect(subscription).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            id: expect.stringMatching(/^sub_/),
            customer_id: "cus_1",
            variant_id: "variant_1",
            quantity: 2,
            interval: "monthly",
            status: "active",
            payment_provider_id: "pp_stripe_stripe",
            payment_method_id: "pm_123",
            canceled_at: null,
            failed_at: null,
            failure_reason: null,
          })
        )
      })

      it("should reject an unknown interval", async () => {
        const error = await service
          .createSubscriptions({
            ...subscriptionData,
            interval: "daily" as any,
          })
          .catch((e) => e)

        expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error)
      })

      it("should list active subscriptions that are due", async () => {
        const [due, notDue, canceled] = await service.createSubscriptions([
          {
            ...subscriptionData,
            next_billing_at: new Date("2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z"),
          },
          {
            ...subscriptionData,
            next_billing_at: new Date("2026-12-01T00:00:00.000Z"),
          },
          {
            ...subscriptionData,
            next_billing_at: new Date("2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z"),
            status: SubscriptionStatus.CANCELED,
          },
        ])

        const subscriptions = await service.listSubscriptions({
          status: SubscriptionStatus.ACTIVE,
          next_billing_at: { $lte: new Date("2026-10-06T00:00:00.000Z") },
        })

        expect(subscriptions.map((s) => s.id)).toEqual([due.id])
        expect([notDue.id, canceled.id]).not.toContain(subscriptions[0].id)
      })

      it("should record a failure", async () => {
        const subscription = await service.createSubscriptions(subscriptionData)
        const failedAt = new Date()

        const updated = await service.updateSubscriptions({
          id: subscription.id,
          status: SubscriptionStatus.FAILED,
          failed_at: failedAt,
          failure_reason: "Payment authorization failed",
        })

        expect(updated).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            status: "failed",
            failed_at: failedAt,
            failure_reason: "Payment authorization failed",
          })
        )
      })
    })
  },
})
```

```text
export const authorizePaymentSessionStep = createStep(
  authorizePaymentSessionStepId,
  async (input: AuthorizePaymentSessionStepInput, { container }) => {
    let payment: PaymentDTO | null | undefined
    const logger = container.resolve<Logger>(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LOGGER)
    const paymentModule = container.resolve<IPaymentModuleService>(
      Modules.PAYMENT
    )

    if (!input.id) {
      return new StepResponse(null)
    }

    try {
      payment = await paymentModule.authorizePaymentSession(
        input.id,
        input.context || {}
      )
    } catch (e) {
      logger.error(
        `Error was thrown trying to authorize payment session - ${input.id} - ${e}`
      )
      // this implies the error is already a MedusaError, so we can throw it safely,
      if (MedusaError.isMedusaError(e)) {
        throw e
      }
      
    }

    const paymentSession = await paymentModule.retrievePaymentSession(
      input.id,
      {
        relations: ["payment", "payment.captures"],
      }
    )

    // If the payment authorization is deferred (e.g., bank transfer, payment link),
    // allow the workflow to proceed without a payment record.
    if (
      paymentSession.status === PaymentSessionStatus.PENDING_AUTHORIZATION
    ) {
      return new StepResponse(null)
    }

    // Throw a special error type when the status is requires_more as it requires a specific further action
    // from the consumer
    if (paymentSession.status === PaymentSessionStatus.REQUIRES_MORE) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.PAYMENT_REQUIRES_MORE_ERROR,
        `More information is required for payment`
      )
    }

    // If any other error other than requires_more shows up, this usually requires the consumer to create a new payment session
    // This could also be a system error thats caused by invalid setup or a failure in connecting to external providers
    if (paymentSession.status !== PaymentSessionStatus.AUTHORIZED || !payment) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.PAYMENT_AUTHORIZATION_ERROR,
        `Payment authorization failed`
      )
    }

    return new StepResponse(paymentSession.payment)
```

```bash
import type {
  CustomerDTO,
  ISubscriptionModuleService,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  MedusaError,
  Modules,
  SUBSCRIPTION_INTERVAL_METADATA_KEY,
  SubscriptionInterval,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { createStep } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"

/**
 * The details of the line items and customer to validate.
 */
export interface ValidateSubscriptionItemsStepInput {
  /**
   * The line items to validate. Only items whose metadata has a
   * `subscription_interval` are validated.
   */
  items: {
    /**
     * The ID of the item's variant.
     */
    variant_id?: string | null
    /**
     * The item's metadata.
     */
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
  }[]
  /**
   * The customer that will own the subscriptions. Only checked when
   * `require_customer` is enabled.
   */
  customer?: Pick<CustomerDTO, "id" | "has_account"> | null
  /**
   * Whether the subscription items require a registered customer.
   */
  require_customer?: boolean
}

export const validateSubscriptionItemsStepId = "validate-subscription-items"
/**
 * This step validates line items that are bought as a subscription. It throws
 * an error if an item's interval isn't one of the intervals in its variant's
 * subscription plan, or if a registered customer is required but missing.
 *
 * @example
 * validateSubscriptionItemsStep({
 *   items: [
 *     {
 *       variant_id: "variant_123",
 *       metadata: { subscription_interval: "monthly" },
 *     },
 *   ],
 * })
 */
export const validateSubscriptionItemsStep = createStep(
  validateSubscriptionItemsStepId,
  async (input: ValidateSubscriptionItemsStepInput, { container }) => {
    const subscriptionItems = (input.items ?? []).filter((item) =>
      isSubscriptionItem(item)
    )

    if (!subscriptionItems.length) {
      return
    }

    if (input.require_customer && !input.customer?.has_account) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
        "A registered customer is required to purchase a subscription"
      )
    }

    const validIntervals = Object.values(SubscriptionInterval) as string[]
    for (const item of subscriptionItems) {
      const interval = item.metadata![SUBSCRIPTION_INTERVAL_METADATA_KEY]
      if (!validIntervals.includes(interval as string)) {
        throw new MedusaError(
          MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
          `Invalid subscription interval: ${interval}`
        )
      }
    }

    const subscriptionModule = container.resolve<ISubscriptionModuleService>(
      Modules.SUBSCRIPTION
    )
    const variantIds = subscriptionItems.map((item) => item.variant_id!)
    const plans = await subscriptionModule.listSubscriptionPlans({
      variant_id: variantIds,
    })
    const plansByVariant = new Map(plans.map((plan) => [plan.variant_id, plan]))

    for (const item of subscriptionItems) {
      const interval = item.metadata![SUBSCRIPTION_INTERVAL_METADATA_KEY]
      const plan = plansByVariant.get(item.variant_id!)

      if (!plan || !(plan.intervals as string[]).includes(interval as string)) {
        throw new MedusaError(
          MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
          `Variant ${item.variant_id} can't be purchased as a ${interval} subscription`
        )
      }
    }
  }
)

/**
 * Whether a line item is bought as a subscription.
 */
export function isSubscriptionItem(item: {
  variant_id?: string | null
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
}): boolean {
  return (
    !!item.variant_id &&
    item.metadata?.[SUBSCRIPTION_INTERVAL_METADATA_KEY] !== undefined &&
    item.metadata?.[SUBSCRIPTION_INTERVAL_METADATA_KEY] !== null
  )
}
EOF
cat > steps/create-subscriptions-from-cart.ts <<'EOF'
import type {
  CartWorkflowDTO,
  CreateSubscriptionDTO,
  ISubscriptionModuleService,
  LinkDefinition,
  PaymentDTO,
  SubscriptionIntervalType,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  computeNextBillingDate,
  ContainerRegistrationKeys,
  MedusaError,
  Modules,
  SUBSCRIPTION_INTERVAL_METADATA_KEY,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { createStep, StepResponse } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { isSubscriptionItem } from "./validate-subscription-items"

/**
 * The ID of the system payment provider. It doesn't charge customers, so it
 * doesn't need a saved payment method to renew a subscription.
 */
const SYSTEM_PAYMENT_PROVIDER_ID = "pp_system_default"

/**
 * The details of the completed cart to create subscriptions from.
 */
export interface CreateSubscriptionsFromCartStepInput {
  /**
   * The completed cart.
   */
  cart: Pick<CartWorkflowDTO, "id" | "items" | "customer">
  /**
   * The ID of the order created from the cart.
   */
  order_id: string
  /**
   * The payment authorized for the order.
   */
  payment: Pick<PaymentDTO, "provider_id" | "data"> | null
}

export const createSubscriptionsFromCartStepId = "create-subscriptions-from-cart"
/**
 * This step creates a subscription for each line item in a completed cart that
 * was bought as a subscription, and links each subscription to the order.
 *
 * The authorized payment must hold a payment method saved for off-session use,
 * which is used to charge renewals. For Stripe, the payment session must be
 * created with `setup_future_usage: "off_session"` in its `data`.
 *
 * @example
 * const subscriptions = createSubscriptionsFromCartStep({
 *   cart,
 *   order_id: "order_123",
 *   payment,
 * })
 */
export const createSubscriptionsFromCartStep = createStep(
  createSubscriptionsFromCartStepId,
  async (input: CreateSubscriptionsFromCartStepInput, { container }) => {
    const subscriptionItems = (input.cart.items ?? []).filter((item) =>
      isSubscriptionItem(item)
    )

    if (!subscriptionItems.length) {
      return new StepResponse([], { subscriptionIds: [], links: [] })
    }

    const customerId = input.cart.customer?.id
    if (!customerId) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
        "A registered customer is required to purchase a subscription"
      )
    }

    if (!input.payment) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
        "An authorized payment is required to purchase a subscription"
      )
    }

    const paymentMethodId = getSavedPaymentMethodId(input.payment)

    const now = new Date()
    const subscriptionsData: CreateSubscriptionDTO[] = subscriptionItems.map(
      (item) => {
        const interval = item.metadata![
          SUBSCRIPTION_INTERVAL_METADATA_KEY
        ] as SubscriptionIntervalType

        return {
          customer_id: customerId,
          variant_id: item.variant_id!,
          quantity: Number(item.quantity),
          interval,
          next_billing_at: computeNextBillingDate(now, interval),
          payment_provider_id: input.payment!.provider_id,
          payment_method_id: paymentMethodId,
        }
      }
    )

    const subscriptionModule = container.resolve<ISubscriptionModuleService>(
      Modules.SUBSCRIPTION
    )
    const link = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LINK)

    const subscriptions = await subscriptionModule.createSubscriptions(
      subscriptionsData
    )

    const links: LinkDefinition[] = subscriptions.map((subscription) => ({
      [Modules.ORDER]: { order_id: input.order_id },
      [Modules.SUBSCRIPTION]: { subscription_id: subscription.id },
    }))

    try {
      await link.create(links)
    } catch (e) {
      await subscriptionModule.deleteSubscriptions(
        subscriptions.map((subscription) => subscription.id)
      )
      throw e
    }

    return new StepResponse(subscriptions, {
      subscriptionIds: subscriptions.map((subscription) => subscription.id),
      links,
    })
  },
  async (data, { container }) => {
    if (!data?.subscriptionIds.length) {
      return
    }

    const subscriptionModule = container.resolve<ISubscriptionModuleService>(
      Modules.SUBSCRIPTION
    )
    const link = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.LINK)

    await link.dismiss(data.links)
    await subscriptionModule.deleteSubscriptions(data.subscriptionIds)
  }
)

/**
 * Returns the ID of the payment method saved for off-session use in an
 * authorized payment. Throws if a provider that charges customers didn't
 * save one, since renewals couldn't be charged.
 */
function getSavedPaymentMethodId(
  payment: Pick<PaymentDTO, "provider_id" | "data">
): string | null {
  if (payment.provider_id === SYSTEM_PAYMENT_PROVIDER_ID) {
    return null
  }

  const data = (payment.data ?? {}) as Record<string, any>
  const paymentMethod = data.payment_method
  const paymentMethodId =
    typeof paymentMethod === "string" ? paymentMethod : paymentMethod?.id

  if (!paymentMethodId || data.setup_future_usage !== "off_session") {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
      `A subscription requires a payment method saved for off-session use. Create the payment session with "setup_future_usage": "off_session" in its data.`
    )
  }

  return paymentMethodId
}
EOF
```

```bash
import type {

  UpdateSubscriptionPlanDTO,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { createStep, StepResponse } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"

/**
 * The subscription plans to update.
 */
export type UpdateSubscriptionPlansStepInput = UpdateSubscriptionPlanDTO[]

export const updateSubscriptionPlansStepId = "update-subscription-plans"
/**
 * This step updates one or more subscription plans.
 *
 * @example
 * const plans = updateSubscriptionPlansStep([
 *   { id: "subplan_123", intervals: ["monthly", "yearly"] },
 * ])
 */
export const updateSubscriptionPlansStep = createStep(
  updateSubscriptionPlansStepId,
  async (data: UpdateSubscriptionPlansStepInput, { container }) => {
    const service = container.resolve<ISubscriptionModuleService>(
      Modules.SUBSCRIPTION
    )

    const previous = await service.listSubscriptionPlans({
      id: data.map((plan) => plan.id),
    })

    const updated = await service.updateSubscriptionPlans(data)

    return new StepResponse(
      updated,
      previous.map((plan) => ({ id: plan.id, intervals: plan.intervals }))
    )
  },
  async (previous, { container }) => {
    if (!previous?.length) {
      return
    }

    const service = container.resolve<ISubscriptionModuleService>(
      Modules.SUBSCRIPTION
    )

    await service.updateSubscriptionPlans(previous)
  }
)

  deleteSubscriptionPlansStepId,

      Modules.SUBSCRIPTION

    await service.softDeleteSubscriptionPlans(ids)

import type {
  ISubscriptionModuleService,
  UpdateSubscriptionDTO,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { createStep, StepResponse } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"

/**
 * The subscriptions to update.
 */
export type UpdateSubscriptionsStepInput = UpdateSubscriptionDTO[]

export const updateSubscriptionsStepId = "update-subscriptions"
/**
 * This step updates one or more subscriptions.
 *
 * @example
 * const subscriptions = updateSubscriptionsStep([
 *   { id: "sub_123", status: "canceled", canceled_at: new Date() },
 * ])
 */
export const updateSubscriptionsStep = createStep(
  updateSubscriptionsStepId,
  async (data: UpdateSubscriptionsStepInput, { container }) => {
    const service = container.resolve<ISubscriptionModuleService>(
      Modules.SUBSCRIPTION
    )

    const previous = await service.listSubscriptions({
      id: data.map((subscription) => subscription.id),
    })

    const updated = await service.updateSubscriptions(data)

    return new StepResponse(
      updated,
      previous.map((subscription) => ({
        id: subscription.id,
        status: subscription.status,
        next_billing_at: subscription.next_billing_at,
        canceled_at: subscription.canceled_at,
        failed_at: subscription.failed_at,
        failure_reason: subscription.failure_reason,
      }))
    )
  },
  async (previous, { container }) => {
    if (!previous?.length) {
      return
    }

    const service = container.resolve<ISubscriptionModuleService>(
      Modules.SUBSCRIPTION
    )

    await service.updateSubscriptions(previous)
  }
)
EOF

import type { SubscriptionDTO } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { MedusaError, SubscriptionStatus } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { createStep } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"

/**
 * The details of the subscription to validate.
 */
export interface ValidateSubscriptionCancelationStepInput {
  /**
   * The subscription to cancel.
   */
  subscription: Pick<SubscriptionDTO, "id" | "customer_id" | "status">
  /**
   * The ID of the customer canceling the subscription. If set, the
   * subscription must belong to this customer.
   */
  customer_id?: string
}

export const validateSubscriptionCancelationStepId =
  "validate-subscription-cancelation"
/**
 * This step validates that a subscription can be canceled. It throws an error
 * if the subscription belongs to a different customer or isn't active.
 *
 * @example
 * validateSubscriptionCancelationStep({
 *   subscription,
 *   customer_id: "cus_123",
 * })
 */
export const validateSubscriptionCancelationStep = createStep(
  validateSubscriptionCancelationStepId,
  async (input: ValidateSubscriptionCancelationStepInput) => {
    const { subscription, customer_id } = input

    if (customer_id && subscription.customer_id !== customer_id) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
        `Subscription with id: ${subscription.id} was not found`
      )
    }

    if (subscription.status !== SubscriptionStatus.ACTIVE) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
        `Subscription with id: ${subscription.id} is ${subscription.status} and can't be canceled`
      )
    }
  }
)
EOF
```

```bash
import type {
  SubscriptionIntervalType,
  SubscriptionPlanDTO,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  createWorkflow,
  transform,
  when,
  WorkflowData,
  WorkflowResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { useQueryGraphStep } from "../../common"
import { createSubscriptionPlansStep } from "../steps/create-subscription-plans"
import { updateSubscriptionPlansStep } from "../steps/update-subscription-plans"

/**
 * The subscription plan to create or update for a variant.
 */
export type UpsertSubscriptionPlanWorkflowInput = {
  /**
   * The ID of the product variant.
   */
  variant_id: string
  /**
   * The intervals a customer can subscribe to the variant at.
   */
  intervals: SubscriptionIntervalType[]
}

export const upsertSubscriptionPlanWorkflowId = "upsert-subscription-plan"
/**
 * This workflow makes a product variant available as a subscription by
 * creating its subscription plan, or updates the intervals of its existing
 * plan. It's used by the Upsert Subscription Plan Admin API Route.
 *
 * @example
 * const { result } = await upsertSubscriptionPlanWorkflow(container)
 * .run({
 *   input: {
 *     variant_id: "variant_123",
 *     intervals: ["monthly", "yearly"],
 *   }
 * })
 *
 * @summary
 *
 * Create or update a variant's subscription plan.
 */
export const upsertSubscriptionPlanWorkflow = createWorkflow(
  upsertSubscriptionPlanWorkflowId,
  (input: WorkflowData<UpsertSubscriptionPlanWorkflowInput>) => {
    useQueryGraphStep({
      entity: "product_variant",
      fields: ["id"],
      filters: { id: input.variant_id },
      options: { throwIfKeyNotFound: true },
    }).config({ name: "get-variant" })

    const { data: existingPlans } = useQueryGraphStep({
      entity: "subscription_plan",
      fields: ["id"],
      filters: { variant_id: input.variant_id },
    }).config({ name: "get-subscription-plan" })

    const existingPlanId = transform({ existingPlans }, ({ existingPlans }) => {
      return existingPlans[0]?.id as string | undefined
    })

    const updated = when(
      "update-subscription-plan",
      { existingPlanId },
      ({ existingPlanId }) => !!existingPlanId
    ).then(() => {
      return updateSubscriptionPlansStep([
        { id: existingPlanId!, intervals: input.intervals },
      ])
    })

    const created = when(
      "create-subscription-plan",
      { existingPlanId },
      ({ existingPlanId }) => !existingPlanId
    ).then(() => {
      return createSubscriptionPlansStep([
        { variant_id: input.variant_id, intervals: input.intervals },
      ])
    })

    const plan = transform({ updated, created }, ({ updated, created }) => {
      return (updated?.[0] ?? created?.[0]) as SubscriptionPlanDTO
    })

    return new WorkflowResponse(plan)
  }
)
EOF

import {
  createWorkflow,
  transform,
  WorkflowData,
  WorkflowResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { useQueryGraphStep } from "../../common"
import { deleteSubscriptionPlansStep } from "../steps/delete-subscription-plans"

/**
 * The variant whose subscription plan to delete.
 */
export type DeleteSubscriptionPlanWorkflowInput = {
  /**
   * The ID of the product variant.
   */
  variant_id: string
}

export const deleteSubscriptionPlanWorkflowId = "delete-subscription-plan"
/**
 * This workflow deletes a variant's subscription plan, so the variant can no
 * longer be purchased as a new subscription. Existing subscriptions to the
 * variant keep renewing. It's used by the Delete Subscription Plan Admin API
 * Route.
 *
 * @example
 * await deleteSubscriptionPlanWorkflow(container)
 * .run({
 *   input: {
 *     variant_id: "variant_123",
 *   }
 * })
 *
 * @summary
 *
 * Delete a variant's subscription plan.
 */
export const deleteSubscriptionPlanWorkflow = createWorkflow(
  deleteSubscriptionPlanWorkflowId,
  (input: WorkflowData<DeleteSubscriptionPlanWorkflowInput>) => {
    const { data: plans } = useQueryGraphStep({
      entity: "subscription_plan",
      fields: ["id"],
      filters: { variant_id: input.variant_id },
    })

    const planIds = transform({ plans }, ({ plans }) =>
      plans.map((plan) => plan.id as string)
    )

    deleteSubscriptionPlansStep(planIds)

    return new WorkflowResponse(void 0)
  }
)

import type { SubscriptionDTO } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { SubscriptionStatus } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import {
  createWorkflow,
  transform,
  WorkflowData,
  WorkflowResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { useQueryGraphStep } from "../../common"
import { updateSubscriptionsStep } from "../steps/update-subscriptions"
import { validateSubscriptionCancelationStep } from "../steps/validate-subscription-cancelation"

/**
 * The subscription to cancel.
 */
export type CancelSubscriptionWorkflowInput = {
  /**
   * The ID of the subscription.
   */
  id: string
  /**
   * The ID of the customer canceling the subscription. If set, the
   * subscription must belong to this customer.
   */
  customer_id?: string
}

export const cancelSubscriptionWorkflowId = "cancel-subscription"
/**
 * This workflow cancels an active subscription immediately, so it isn't
 * renewed again. It's used by the Cancel Subscription Store API Route.
 *
 * @example
 * const { result } = await cancelSubscriptionWorkflow(container)
 * .run({
 *   input: {
 *     id: "sub_123",
 *     customer_id: "cus_123",
 *   }
 * })
 *
 * @summary
 *
 * Cancel a subscription.
 */
export const cancelSubscriptionWorkflow = createWorkflow(
  cancelSubscriptionWorkflowId,
  (input: WorkflowData<CancelSubscriptionWorkflowInput>) => {
    const { data: subscription } = useQueryGraphStep({
      entity: "subscription",
      fields: ["id", "customer_id", "status"],
      filters: { id: input.id },
      options: { throwIfKeyNotFound: true, isList: false },
    })

    validateSubscriptionCancelationStep({
      subscription,
      customer_id: input.customer_id,
    })

    const updateData = transform({ input }, ({ input }) => [
      {
        id: input.id,
        status: SubscriptionStatus.CANCELED,
        canceled_at: new Date(),
      },
    ])

    const [canceled] = updateSubscriptionsStep(updateData)

    return new WorkflowResponse(canceled as SubscriptionDTO)
  }
)
```
